mainTopic: Fresh and dried figs for תרומה (measuring size, and which to give with or without a כהן), then the משנה on keeping מנחות, even their שיריים, from becoming חמץ.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a comparison: just as תרומה גדולה is given generously (בעין יפה), so too is תרומת מעשר. The גמרא tries to prove from רבי יוסי's practice, giving ten dried figs for ninety fresh ones, that produce is measured by its original size. רבי אלעזר rejects the proof, because dried figs are special: boiling brings them back to their fresh size. A ברייתא then rules that fresh figs may be given for dried figs where people usually dry figs, but dried figs may never be given for fresh ones. The גמרא explains that the first half is a case with no כהן present, where you give what lasts. The second half is a case with a כהן present, where you give the best. From this רב פפא learns a general rule: we would rather read a teaching as one תנא describing two cases than split it between two תנאים. A new משנה then teaches that מנחות must be kept from becoming חמץ, even their שיריים, with liability for kneading, shaping and baking. ריש לקיש brings the source from ״לא תאפה חמץ חלקם״, and the גמרא begins to challenge it, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Giving תרומת מעשר generously, like תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: The comparison between תרומת מעשר and תרומה גדולה teaches that both are given generously.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and by thought. Just as תרומה גדולה is given with a generous eye, so too תרומת מעשר is given with a generous eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a comparison that began before this section. Because תרומת מעשר is compared to תרומה גדולה, we also learn that תרומת מעשר should be given generously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison already taught that תרומת מעשר, like תרומה גדולה, can be separated by estimate and by thought. Now it adds a second lesson: it should be given בעין יפה, with a generous hand. This prepares the next step, which looks at a case where someone gave dried figs for fresh ones.

keyTerms.meaning: The main תרומה that the owner gives to the כהן from his produce
The tenth of his מעשר that the לוי gives to the כהן
With a generous eye, giving freely and not stingily
Thought, meaning separating by deciding in one's mind

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמַחְשָׁבָה, מָה תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּעַיִן יָפָה,
phrases.english: and by thought. Just as standard teruma is with a generous eye,
phrases.notes: The word 'and by thought' finishes a line from just before this: תרומה can be separated by estimate and by thought.

phrases.english: so too teruma of the tithe is with a generous eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּעַיִן יָפָה, אַף תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר בְּעַיִן יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison of תרומת מעשר to תרומה גדולה from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומת מעשר, like תרומה גדולה, should be given generously.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי's practice with dried figs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי separated ten dried figs for ninety fresh ones, which seems to prove we measure by the original size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this we can prove it. רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי said: Father would take ten dried figs from the drying container for ninety fresh figs in the basket. If you say we measure by how they were originally, that works. But if you say we measure by how they are now, the dried figs are too few.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report about רבי יוסי to prove that produce is measured by its original size (לכמות שהן).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten out of a hundred is the right share for תרומת מעשר. But ten dried figs are much smaller than ten fresh figs. If size were measured as they are now (כמות שהן), רבי יוסי gave too little. His practice only makes sense if the dried figs count at their original fresh size.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried figs
A container where figs are laid out to dry
A basket
As they were, meaning by their original size
As they are, meaning by their size right now
Is lacking, is too little

phrases.english: And from this [there is a proof]:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
Father would take ten dried figs
that were in the vessel, for ninety that were in the basket.
phrases.notes: The ninety in the basket are fresh figs. The גמרא doesn't say it outright, but the whole proof depends on it.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
we go by how they were, it is fine,
but if you say [we go by] how they are now,
they are too few.
phrases.notes: Ten shrunken dried figs take up less space than ten fresh ones, so they would fall short of the required share.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the theme of measuring תרומת מעשר to a real case, to decide whether size is measured now or originally.
steps.raayaObject: That produce is measured by its original size (לכמות שהן).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי's report that his father gave ten dried figs for ninety fresh ones.

steps.title: Dried figs are a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that dried figs are different because boiling brings them back to their original size.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Dried figs are different, since one can boil them and bring them back to how they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the previous step. רבי יוסי's practice works only because dried figs have a special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dried figs can be boiled and swell back to their fresh size, so they are treated as if they were still fresh. This is a special feature of figs. It does not prove a general rule that all produce is measured by its original size.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, used to set a case apart as special
Since, because
To boil them
To bring them back, to restore them

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Dried figs are different,
since one can boil them
and return them to how they were.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שָׁאנֵי גְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the fig case as proof for a general rule of לכמות שהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Dried figs can be boiled back to full size, so they are a special case and cannot teach a rule for other foods.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's practice with dried figs does not prove that all produce is measured by its original size. Figs are special because boiling brings them back to their old size.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב דימי is saying we always measure by original size. He is only saying that figs are a special case, because boiling restores them, so they cannot prove a general rule for other foods.

steps.title: ברייתא on separating fresh figs for dried figs
steps.stepSummary: Fresh figs may be separated for dried figs where people normally dry figs. Dried figs may never be separated for fresh ones, even in such a place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We may separate תרומה from fresh figs for dried figs in a place where people usually make fresh figs into dried figs. But we may not separate dried figs for fresh figs, even in a place where people usually make fresh figs into dried figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It sets the rules for separating תרומה between fresh figs and dried figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating fresh for dried is allowed only where people commonly dry figs. Separating dried for fresh is forbidden everywhere, even in that kind of place. The ברייתא sets up a one-way rule, and the גמרא will need to work with the difference between the two directions.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate תרומה
Fresh figs
Are used to doing, usually do

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We may separate teruma from fresh figs for dried figs,
in a place where they are accustomed
to make fresh figs into dried figs,
but not dried figs for fresh figs,
even in a place where they are accustomed
to make fresh figs into dried figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תּוֹרְמִין תְּאֵנִים עַל הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new source about fresh and dried figs, which continues the theme of the previous steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fresh figs may be separated for dried figs where drying figs is common. Dried figs may not be separated for fresh figs anywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule works in only one direction. This sets up the next discussion about how fresh and dried produce relate for תרומה.

steps.title: Quoting the figs ruling and drawing an inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first half of the ברייתא again. It infers that fresh figs may be given for dried ones only where people usually dry figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: You may give fresh figs as תרומה for dried figs in a place where people usually dry figs. So where people dry figs, yes. Where they don't, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again so it can study it closely. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only allows it 'in a place where people dry figs.' So the גמרא reads the opposite as well: where people don't dry figs, you may not give fresh figs for dried ones. This inference is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Where people are not used to it, where it is not the normal practice

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: תּוֹרְמִין תְּאֵנִים עַל הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת
phrases.english: The Master said: One may separate תרומה from fresh figs for dried figs
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא we saw in Step 4, quoted again so the גמרא can look at it closely.

phrases.english: in a place where they are used to making fresh figs into dried figs.
In a place where they are used to it — yes,
in a place where they are not used to it — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: תּוֹרְמִין תְּאֵנִים עַל הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 4 to examine it closely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fresh figs may be given for dried figs only where people usually dry figs. Elsewhere it is not allowed.

steps.title: It can't be a case with a כהן present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ruling is about. If a כהן is there, fresh figs should be allowed everywhere, because we give the best produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If a כהן is there, why not allow it even where people don't dry figs? We learned in a משנה that when a כהן is present, you give from the best.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא is describing. It shows that 'a כהן is present' can't be the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh figs are better quality than dried ones. When a כהן is present, he can eat them right away, and the משנה says to give the best. If so, fresh figs should be allowed everywhere, not only where people dry figs.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
There is / is present
Why?
From the best-quality produce

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If there is a priest present,
then in a place where they are not used to it, why not?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: מְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּהֵן תּוֹרֵם מִן הַיָּפֶה!
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: In a place where there is a priest, one separates from the best!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in תרומות 2:4. Fresh figs count as 'the best' here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible reading of the inference from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the first half of the ברייתא is about a case where a כהן is present.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When a כהן is present, the משנה says to give the best. Fresh figs are the best, so they should be allowed in every place.

steps.title: So the first half must be a case with no כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the first half of the ברייתא is about a case where no כהן is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that there is no כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'כהן present' reading doesn't work, the גמרא switches to 'no כהן present.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no כהן around, the תרומה has to wait, and fresh figs might spoil. Where people dry figs, the fresh figs can be dried and will last, so it is allowed only there. This explains the limit in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the first option)
It is obvious / it must be
There is not / is not present

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that there is no priest present,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in Step 6 by changing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might have been about a case with a כהן present.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first half is about a case with no כהן present, where the produce needs to last.

steps.title: The second half doesn't fit a case with no כהן
steps.stepSummary: The second half bans giving dried figs for fresh ones. With no כהן present, the dried figs, which last longer, should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the second half: not dried figs for fresh figs, even where people dry figs. If there is no כהן, why not? We learned that when no כהן is present, you give from what lasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the 'no כהן' reading against the second half of the ברייתא and finds a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה says that without a כהן, you give the produce that lasts. Dried figs last, so they should be allowed. The ברייתא bans them, which means the 'no כהן' reading can't work for the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause (look at the end of the source)
The produce that lasts / keeps well

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
but not dried figs for fresh figs,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁרָגִיל לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּאֵנִים גְּרוֹגְרוֹת.
phrases.english: even in a place where they are used to making fresh figs into dried figs.
And if there is no priest present, why not?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן – תּוֹרֵם מִן הַמִּתְקַיֵּים!
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: In a place where there is no priest, one separates from what lasts!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וְלֹא גְּרוֹגְרוֹת עַל הַתְּאֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from Step 7 using the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the whole ברייתא as a case where no כהן is present.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a כהן, you give what lasts. Dried figs last, so banning them doesn't fit.

steps.title: So the second half must be a case with a כהן present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the second half is about a case where a כהן is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that there is a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying that the second half describes a case where a כהן is present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כהן present, you give the best, and fresh figs are better than dried ones. So giving dried figs for fresh ones is not allowed, even where people dry figs.

keyTerms.meaning: Where a כהן is present

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that there is a priest present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in Step 8 by changing the case for the second half.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second half might also be a case with no כהן present.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second half is about a case with a כהן present, where the best produce must be given.

steps.title: Can the two halves be different cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it makes sense for the first half to be a case with no כהן and the second half a case with a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first half is with no כהן, and the second half is with a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that its answers leave the ברייתא split into two different situations, and asks whether that can be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we expect one ברייתא to describe a single case. Here each half had to be explained as a different case, so the גמרא questions it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause (beginning of the source)
The latter clause (end of the source)

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא דְּלֵיכָּא כֹּהֵן, סֵיפָא דְּאִיכָּא כֹּהֵן?
phrases.english: The first clause is where there is no priest, and the latter clause is where there is a priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא דְּלֵיכָּא כֹּהֵן, סֵיפָא דְּאִיכָּא כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the combined result of Steps 7 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the two halves of the ברייתא as two different cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems strange for one ברייתא to switch situations in the middle without saying so.

steps.title: Yes, the two halves are different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the split: the first half is a case with no כהן present, and the second half is a case with a כהן present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, the first half is with no כהן, and the second half is with a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply says 'yes.' The ברייתא really does describe two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is changed or pushed back. The גמרא agrees that each half follows a different rule from the משנה: 'what lasts' for the first half and 'the best' for the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

steps.whatToRemember: When a כהן is present, give the best: fresh figs win, and dried figs may never be given for fresh ones. When no כהן is present, give what lasts: fresh figs are allowed for dried ones only where people dry figs, since they can be dried and will keep.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין' here is the Aramaic word for 'yes.' It is not the Hebrew word אין that means 'there is not.'

phrases.english: Yes, the first clause is where there is no priest present,
and the latter clause is where there is a priest present.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, רֵישָׁא דְּלֵיכָּא כֹּהֵן, סֵיפָא דְּאִיכָּא כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point raised in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's first half is a case with no כהן present (give what lasts), and its second half is a case with a כהן present (give the best).

steps.title: רב פפא's rule: two cases rather than two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the previous discussion that we push to explain a ברייתא as one תנא with two cases, rather than as the view of two different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that we strain to explain a teaching as covering two different situations, but we do not explain it as coming from two different תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sums up the lesson of the whole discussion we just finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא explained the first half of the ברייתא as a case with no כהן present and the second half as a case with a כהן present. That is a bit forced. רב פפא says this tells us something general: we would rather force two cases into one teaching than say the halves were taught by two different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: we strain or push ourselves to find an explanation
we set up or explain a text as talking about a certain case
two reasons, meaning two different situations
two different תנאים who disagree

steps.whatToRemember: A text is assumed to come from one author. We prefer to read it as one תנא describing two cases, even if that is a stretch, rather than splitting it between two תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading משניות and ברייתות all through ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this
that we strain and explain the teaching
according to two reasons
phrases.notes: He means two different situations, like 'no כהן present' and 'a כהן present' in the steps before this.

phrases.english: but we do not explain it as the view of two תנאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule for reading texts from the split explanation accepted in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Reading a text as one תנא with two cases is better than splitting it between two תנאים.

steps.title: New משנה: guarding meal-offerings from becoming leaven
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that מנחות are kneaded with lukewarm water and guarded from becoming חמץ. If even the שיריים become חמץ, one breaks a לא תעשה, and one is liable for kneading, shaping and baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the מנחות are kneaded with lukewarm water, and one watches them so they do not become חמץ. If even the leftover part became חמץ, one breaks a prohibition, because the פסוק says that no מנחה brought to ה׳ may be made חמץ. One is liable for kneading it, for shaping it, and for baking it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching the rules for keeping a מנחה from becoming חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds two points. The ban on חמץ applies even to the שיריים, the part the כהנים eat. Also, each step of making the dough (kneading, shaping, baking) counts as a separate act one can be liable for.

keyTerms.meaning: meal-offerings made of flour
lukewarm water
the leftover part of a מנחה that the כהנים eat after the קומץ is removed
a negative commandment, a prohibition
kneading, shaping, baking

steps.confusionAlert: The שיריים are never burned on the מזבח. Still, the משנה says they too may not become חמץ.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the meal-offerings
are kneaded with lukewarm water
and one watches over them so that they do not become leaven
and if its remainder became leaven,
one violates a prohibition
as it is said: "No meal-offering that you bring to the Lord
shall be made with leaven"
and one is liable for its kneading
and for its shaping, and for its baking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחות must be guarded from חמץ. Even the שיריים becoming חמץ breaks a לא תעשה, with liability for kneading, shaping and baking.

steps.title: Source for the leftovers rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that even the שיריים may not become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up ריש לקיש's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק quoted in the משנה speaks about the מנחה brought to ה׳. It is not clear from it that the שיריים, which the כהנים eat, are included. So the גמרא wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the rule that even the leftovers may not become leaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule about the שיריים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the שיריים may not become חמץ.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'even their portion' may not be baked leaven
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads ״לא תאפה חמץ חלקם״ as one phrase: even the כהנים' portion may not be baked as חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The פסוק says, "It shall not be baked leaven; their portion." Read it this way: even their portion may not be baked leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by bringing a פסוק about the כהנים' portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, "their portion" begins a new phrase in the פסוק. ריש לקיש joins it to the words before it, so the פסוק reads "even their portion shall not be baked leaven." "Their portion" is the שיריים the כהנים eat, so this is the source for the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: a פסוק, a verse
their portion, the share the כהנים eat
it shall not be baked

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: For the verse says:
"It shall not be baked with leaven; their portion"
even their portion
shall not be baked with leaven.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לא תאפה חמץ חלקם״, read as "even their portion shall not be baked leaven."

steps.title: Is this verse needed for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: this פסוק seems to be needed for a different teaching found in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this פסוק really come to teach this? It is needed for what is taught in a ברייתא: "It shall not..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's source and starts to quote a ברייתא that uses the same פסוק for something else. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is already used for one teaching is usually not free to teach another. If the ברייתא needs ״לא תאפה חמץ״ for its own lesson, ריש לקיש cannot also use it for the שיריים.
